Use N-mm-MPa units.
Use Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with small deflection and linear elastic behavior.
Model a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Use structural steel with E = 200000 MPa and constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
Apply a downward point load P = 2000 N at the free end.
Compute EI as 200000 MPa times 1200000 mm^4 equals 2.4 times 10^11 N·mm^2.
Use the standard cantilever point-load formula for the free-end slope: theta = P L^2 / (2 E I).
Use the standard cantilever point-load formula for the free-end vertical deflection: delta = P L^3 / (3 E I).
Calculate the free-end slope as 0.0135 rad, which is approximately 0.774 degrees.
Calculate the free-end vertical deflection as 16.2 mm downward.
Do not use the assumption that the free-end rotation is zero or that the bending moment is constant PL over the full span, because it is physically incorrect for a point load at the free end.
Use the correct bending moment distribution, which varies linearly from -P L at the fixed end to zero at the free end.
